The onset of puberty in this species thus appears tightly coupled to the attainment of a critical body dimension, a pattern observed in many scorpaeniform fishes. Field collections have consistently shown that individuals below this length threshold lack mature oocytes, while those exceeding it are frequently gravid or have recently spawned, confirming that 14 centimeters represents a reliable biometric indicator of reproductive competence for females.
